side_a: CC 4.4.3.4.1: "For a `family` member the admitting host runs the walk after the member is admitted."
side_b: CC 4.4.3.4.4: "A member's substrate re-wraps nothing, because a key grant is sealer-only"
note: Who signs a family catch-up grant: the admitting host re-wraps every earlier DEK it holds (4.4.3.4.1), yet a grant is sealer-only and speaks for the blob's owner (3.1.3, 3.3.2, 4.4.3.4.3 refuses a grant on possession alone); a host-signed wrap of another member's blob is admitted under one reading and refused under the other.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.4.5: "so the first write after the removal is under a key the removed member was never granted"
side_b: CC 5.1: "A removed member's exposure window is therefore `≤ T`, never "until the next scheduled rotation"."
note: 4.4.3.4.5 (the one statement of the removal rule, 'at any scope') gives a removed member nothing new; 5.1 MUST coalesce removals into one rotation per window T (2 s) and lets writes inside T seal under the old epoch. 4.4.3.2.1 makes the community DEK the 5.1 cascade, so the two instants meet on one key. 4.4.3.2.2 and 1.13.3.3 support rotate-before-next-write.

side_a: CC 5.1: "for a kept stream the earlier epochs reach the joiner as `key_grant:stream:v1` wraps, bounded by the catch-up bound below"
side_b: CC 5.3.3.2.5: "a later joiner reads a kept stream only from the epochs whose keys they hold** and nothing earlier"
note: Known, held for Eric; reported because a second reading finds it independently: automatic catch-up wraps against re-share by the publisher only.

side_a: CC 5.1: "Turning kept on mid-stream wraps the current and later epochs."
side_b: CC 5.3.3.2.5: "A publisher changes keep mid-stream at an epoch boundary, as ruled for one DEK per stream per epoch, and the change reaches forward only."
note: 5.1 wraps the epoch already under way (opening its chunks sealed before the change); 5.3.3.2.5 has the change take effect at a boundary and reach forward only. 5.1 itself says turning keep off stops 'from the next epoch'. Little is at stake because an unkept call holds no chunks past forwarding.

side_a: CC 5.4.3: "A newly-added member receives forward keying without retroactive symbol access except as the community's `archive_mode` permits"
side_b: CC 4.4.3.4.1: "A new member at those scopes is granted the current epoch's key at the minter's next sealed write, and no earlier epoch's."
note: 5.4.3 lets archive_mode open retroactive symbol access to a joiner; Part 4 (4.4.3.4.1, 4.4.3.2.6 'confers no grant on an earlier epoch') and CC 3.2 make archive_mode a holder's ageing of its own past-epoch keys, never a grant to a newcomer. The body stays sealed either way.

side_a: CC 3.4.4: "the re-key epoch boundary (CC 4.4.3.4.5) after which the"
side_b: CC 4.4.3.4.5: "so the substrate simply stops wrapping new DEKs to the removed member's keys; no key is reused, so nothing is rotated"
note: The family_membership_change payload calls effective_at on removal 'the re-key epoch boundary (CC 4.4.3.4.5)' and says 'the forward-secrecy re-key' keys on it; at family scope 4.4.3.4.5 and 4.5.12.1 say there is no epoch and no rotation. The wording fits the community analogue only.

side_a: CC 6.1.5.3: "Narrowing withdraws the grants, and the node descends what it no longer has a grant for."
side_b: CC 3.3.2: "a `withdraws` or `recants` naming a `key_grant` row is refused; once shared, always shared at the wire layer"
note: If 'the grants' are key grants (the same section says a node off the list 'receives no keys for the cohort') they cannot be withdrawn; the narrowing can only be the owner's edit of the `cohorts` member plus no new wraps. 'Withdraws' is the verb's name and invites the refused act.

side_a: CC 3.3.2: "No row supersedes or removes the prior wrap."
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json key_grant:{axis} lifecycle: "same_attester (read: lifecycle_predicate attestation_query.rs:760; the door admits any signer's supersedes)"
note: The lifecycle cell (code-v61) gives key_grant a same-attester supersede, while its verbs cell and transitions list attest only and 3.3.2 makes a rotation a new row under a new axis identity, never an edit. The cell should read none.

side_a: CC 3.1.3: "`attesting_key_id` speaks for the content's or stream's owner (`content`, `stream`) or is the epoch's minter"
side_b: data CC 8.10 card key_grant:{axis} (manifests/reactions.json): "@family on admitted(membership:widening): emit `key_grant:content` by identity:substrate_persist"
note: The card's own transition row says the signer is 'member, owner' and its reactions say the catch-up grant is emitted by identity:substrate_persist; the text's sealer speaks for the blob's owner. The same doubt as the admitting-host finding, seen in the data.

side_a: CC 3.3.2: "the row is placed at the content's scope and reaches the recipient's node because the row *refers to* it"
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json key_grant:{axis} replication: ""tier": "federation", "audience": "addressee""
note: The replication cell reads tier federation (audience addressee) from the shipped store; the text and the model's own placement cell put the row at the content's scope. The departure is recorded as open, with no reason.

side_a: CC 3.2: "So a stalled roster admits **exactly one row kind without that count**: a widening whose only change is the addition of a **founder** seat."
side_b: data manifests/transitions.json membership:{stage} attest guard: "when(leaf=widening) (one trust:confers@landed[attested=signer,val:scope=object] else refuse & type(signer,user) else refuse & not type(signer,node) else refuse)"
note: The guard is written for every widening (reach whole, no stalled-and-recovery condition), so as data it refuses any ordinary widening whose signer holds no trust:confers and is not a user key. The text asks this of the one T7 recovery widening only; the change cell beside it carries the condition `widening[stalled&recovery]`, the guard does not. CC 8.10 prints the same guard.

side_a: CC 5.1: "Once a member leaves, subsequent content is sealed under a key that member cannot derive."
side_b: data manifests/transitions.json membership:{stage} attest change: "resignation[scope:self|family]: key=stop_wrap"
note: The change cells rotate the epoch on `removal[scope:community|affiliations]` and stop wraps on a resignation at self or family, and have no cell for a resignation from a community or affiliation (only the ephemeral last-member case). The text rotates on any departure (5.1 'leaves'; 4.5.12.1 'rotation on departure'; CC 3.2 'Resignation and removal are one row kind at the fold'). As data, a member who resigns keeps reading.

side_a: CC 3.1.3.2: "The inviter withdraws a proposal with the ordinary `withdraws`."
side_b: data manifests/transitions.json membership:{stage} withdraw (roles member, source code-v61): ""policy": "cosigned""
note: The family's one withdraw transition is cosigned by members for every stage. The text gives the inviter a lone withdrawal of their own proposal (the registry row calls proposal, acceptance and decline single-signer) and says a growth already admitted is never re-judged, so no cosigned withdraw of a widening exists. The attest row has per-stage policies; the withdraw row has none.

side_a: CC 3.3.6: "No single occurrence evicts at once with no window: that unilateral configuration is one a thief wins in two steps."
side_b: data manifests/transitions.json identity:occurrence withdraw: ""policy": "selfAct""
note: Still present: the withdraw transition of identity:occurrence (roles author, subject) and the attest of identity:occurrence_revocation (roles empty, source gap) both read selfAct, while CC 3.3.6.3 and the CC 3.1.3 carrier row require the two paths, or a strict majority of the live roster for a user self.

side_a: CC 3.1.3.2: "A proposal seats at most once."
side_b: CC 3.2: "The founder's standing **`membership:proposal:v1`** is then addressed to any requester — its `subject_key_ids` is resolved at acceptance rather than fixed at proposal"
note: Read alone, 'a proposal seats at most once' refuses the second joiner on an open room's standing proposal. Condition (5) and the next sentence make the limit per acceptance (P has not already seated K), which is what open admission needs; the short sentence should say so. The 30-day cap on `expires_at` also makes the standing offer one that must be re-issued.

side_a: CC 4.5.12.5: "Unlike self-occurrence, family membership changes are **NOT single-vouch by default**."
side_b: CC 3.3.6.3: "With **two or more** live keys it lands by either path:"
note: 4.5.12.5 and 4.4.3.4.3 ('co-admitted at login by single-vouch') describe a self occurrence as landing on one signature. Since CC 3.3.6.3 that holds only at one key, or for an agent occurrence; at two or more keys a lone signature waits the 86 400 s window. 4.5.12.3 states both; the two short statements predate the door.

side_a: CC 5.3.3.2: "sub-channel members are a subset of the space roster"
side_b: CC 4.4.3.2.7: "Each membership is explicit, ceremony-shaped, and independent."
note: The call table makes a sub-channel's roster a subset of its parent's; no admission predicate in CC 4.4.3.2.3 or CC 3.1.3.2 reads a parent roster, and the multi-level pattern it cites (4.4.3.2.5) states no such check. One reader enforces the subset at a widening, another does not.

side_a: CC 2.1: "Absent means the family's default."
side_b: CC 4.4.3.5.2: "return # no SLA commitment; no watcher"
note: With no deletion commitment on a producer's row, CC 2.1 gives it a default window (so a deadline and a breach exist) and CC 4.4.3.5.2 runs no watcher at all. No default window is stated anywhere, and reactions.json starts the clock only from a `consent:deletion_sla:{days}` row. The watcher also reads the row only: a row carrying the `deletion_window` member and no `deletion_sla` row is watched under CC 3.3.1 ('the member carries the commitment') and not under 4.4.3.5.2.

side_a: CC 3.4.5: "at federation tier the subject MUST hold a live `consent:scope:analyze` grant"
side_b: CC 3.3.1: "A `consent:scope:{kind}` dimension row, if anyone emits one, is **descriptive** — no fold reads it and it confers nothing"
note: Still present: the gate is named by the dimension spelling in the CC 3.4.5 table row, in CC 3.1.8.1 and CC 3.1.4 ('holding a live `consent:scope:analyze` grant'), in CC 4.5.2.2 and in CC 4.5.13 ('a `consent:scope:view` qualifier'). CC 3.3.1 and CC 2.1 make the grant a `consent:state:granted` row whose `scope` member names analyze.

side_a: CC 3.3.1: "pairs with producer's `consent:partnership_accept` via `topical_relation:bilateral_pair`"
side_b: CC 4.4.3.5.3: "recommended, not required for ratification — `bilateral_pair_id` is the binding mechanism"
note: The catalogue row pairs the two halves by a topical_relation edge; CC 2.3.2.4, CC 3.3.5, CC 4.4.3.5.3 and the fold cell (key=bilateral_pair_id) pair them by the envelope member and make the edge optional. A reader of the catalogue row alone finds no pair where the edge is absent.

side_a: CC 1.13.2: "`consent:partnered` is theirs to revoke"
side_b: CC 3.3.1: "The second segment of the dimension (`state`, `stream`, `deletion_sla`, `deletion_complete`, `decay`, `partnership_grant`, `partnership_accept`, `scope`, `replication`, `community_trust`) is exactly the set tabulated below."
note: No leaf `consent:partnered` exists in the closed set; what the person revokes is their `consent:partnership_grant` half (CC 4.4.3.4.3) or the `consent:stream:partnered` bundle. A reader cannot tell which row the foundation sentence means.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.5.5: "if rows is empty: return unspecified // every declaration withdrawn"
side_b: CC 4.4.3.5.5: "revoked if g is null AND R IS NOT NULL"
note: A subject who withdraws their only grant resolves unspecified (as one who never declared); a subject who withdraws the newer of two grants resolves revoked, since the withdrawal sets R and the older grant falls under it. CC 3.3.1's boundary fold gives one answer for both: a revocation or withdrawal stands as a boundary and no grant survives it.

side_a: CC 3.3.1: "the latest admitted revocation's `asserted_at` putting every earlier grant out"
side_b: data CC 8.10 card consent:state:{stance} fold (manifests/family_model.json): "@stance=revoked: cut=terminal"
note: The text of CC 4.4.3.5.5 is repaired to the boundary fold; the data still carries the old reading beside the new one: fold cells `cut=terminal` and `cut=boundary(asserted_at),terminal` cited to CC 4.4.3.5.5, and `pick=rank(revoked>granted)`, under which a revoke outranks a later fresh grant. Executed as written, the terminal cell lets an older unnamed grant stand again. Still present in the data.

side_a: CC 3.3.1: "The node-authored form stays valid, and the fold below groups both forms by `attested_key_id`."
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json consent:community_trust signer_rule and fold: "reads=own&signer:owner"
note: The text admits two authors of a trace-capture grant, the owner and the node itself, and refuses only a key that was neither. The signer cell is `owner_of_subject` alone (closed), the card's attest row says owner, and the fold reads owner-signed rows only, so a node-authored grant is not counted as consent. The verbs cell also lacks recant, which the text gives the attester.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.5.5: "attesting_key_id ∈ delegates_to(s).proxies).where(dimension matches "consent:state:*")"
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json consent:state:{stance} signer_rule: "self | owner_of_subject(for_key_id) x none x {}"
note: The text lets a subject's proxy on a delegates_to chain sign a consent state (CC 3.3.1 step 2, CC 4.4.3.5.5), and the card's fold cell reads `signer:subject|proxy`. The family's signer cell (code-v61) has no delegation arm, while the parent row consent:{kind} gives state `x delegates_to(chain rooted at a subject)`. Two cells of one manifest disagree on whether a proxy's grant is admitted.

side_a: CC 3.3.12: "`content_class` is producer-declared production-class; `cw_class` is community-applied content-warning"
side_b: CC 4.5.13: "This **rides the existing `consent:*` family + a [CC 3.3.12](part_3_the_namespace.md) `content_class:{class}` flag** (`content_class:infohazard` / `content_class:reported`)."
note: The home makes content_class the producer's own description and sends what a community applies to cw_class. The infohazard gate hides content behind a `content_class:reported` flag that follows a community vote, which no producer declares; CC 4.4.3.2.8 also carries an affiliation's sensitivity lattice 'on content_class'. One reader looks for the flag in cw_class from the community, another in content_class from anyone (the data cell is any_registered).

side_a: CC 3.3.13: "The **sender canonicalises before hashing** — which is also what strips EXIF / XMP / ID3 / ICC"
side_b: CC 3.4.14: "A node MUST NOT strip a marking present on ingress."
note: XMP is where an IPTC Digital Source Type or C2PA marking of machine origin arrives in a file. CC 3.3.13 and the CC 5.3.2.6 pipeline ('strip metadata') remove it with no exception; R3 forbids stripping an ingress marking. The two are followed together only if the marking is first lifted onto the row's disclosure field, which neither passage says.

side_a: CC 7.3.4: "Where feasible and appropriate, embed cryptographic provenance watermarks adhering to recognized standards (e.g., C2PA) to ensure authenticity and traceability."
side_b: CC 3.4.14: "that profile's `MAY` is promoted to `MUST` for generated media"
note: Part 7 leaves a C2PA marking to feasibility and has it embedded in the creation; CC 3.4.14 R3 makes the C2PA assertion a MUST at egress for generated media, and CC 3.3.13 declines the embedded manifest inside CEG because it changes the digest. CC 3.4.14 is the normative home; the Part 7 bullet predates it. CC 8.4.2.2 still opens with 'a node MAY emit' before deferring to R3.

side_a: CC 2.1: "A row naming a key outside its audience is refused `subject_outside_audience`."
side_b: data formal/derivation/family_default_row.json subject_rule (manifests/family_model.json, source code-v61): ""in_audience": "no""
note: Still present: the default row and the family cells read from the shipped store say a subject need not be in the audience, while CC 2.1 and CC 5.2 refuse such a row at every targeted scope. To fix in the data.

side_a: CC 4.5.2.1: "`consent:partnered:{user_key}` (the agent-side stance)"
side_b: CC 3.3.1: "A leaf with no named emitter class is unregistered, and a consumer MUST reject it rather than admit it ungated"
note: The subject-bearing pattern list (also CC 2.3.1) requires `subject_key_ids` on a `consent:partnered:{user_key}` row; CC 3.3.1 closes the consent leaves and has no `partnered` leaf, so that row is refused before the subject rule is reached. The partnership rows are `consent:partnership_grant` and `_accept`, whose partner rides the singular `subject_key_id` (CC 4.4.3.4.3.1). The `observed:` and `epistemic:` patterns of the same table name no registered family either.

side_a: CC 2.3.4: "agent attests `identity:current` about itself with `subject_key_ids = [self.key_id]`"
side_b: CC 3.3.2: "Every row carries a registered dimension ([CC 2.4](part_2_the_grammar.md) gate)."
note: The self-consent example uses a dimension no registry row carries (the identity family's leaves are occurrence, occurrence_revocation and canonical_binding); a row emitted as the example shows is refused as unregistered. The rule itself (attester in its own subject list) is unaffected.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.4.3.1: "**the partner** — the OTHER party (agent occurrence for `grant`, user identity for `accept`); singular, non-empty"
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json consent:partnership_grant signer_rule: "a subject of the target, or a chain rooted at one"
note: The text side of C360 is repaired (CC 3.4.5 and CC 3.3.1 now say the granting user signs and the subject is the partner). The data cell still carries the old reading in its qualifier and a `delegates_to(chain rooted at a subject)` arm: read literally the grant is signed by its own subject, the partner. The card's 'self' is right; the qualifier and the arm are stale.
